279666e7f03e84c7760e.en: Newtalk News South Korean Defense Minister Kang Sin-chul told a congressional committee on Tuesday that the explosion last week that injured two South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) was confirmed to have been caused by a North Korean mine. He pointed out that this move is a clear violation of the Korean Armistice Agreement and stressed that Pyongyang must take full responsibility and the South Korean military will also take step-by-step measures. The explosion occurred on Sept. 21, south of the military demarcation line in North Korea's demilitarized zone, according to Reuters. Kang said the mines were apparently planted by North Korea during border fortifications in the region and were intended to clarify whether the North had deliberately planted them in the knowledge that South Korean forces would enter the area. South Korea's Ministry of Defense and the United Nations Command subsequently launched a joint investigation and found an additional piece of North Korean-made resin near the explosion site.

954aea80af232447bede.en: Newtalk News As the Pacific El Niño continues to intensify this year, a massive “Kelvin wave” is moving toward the California coast in the United States, and scientists warn that this invisible ocean wave may temporarily raise sea levels along the California coast by up to about 30 cm, further amplifying the risk of winter storms, storm surges, flooding, and coastal erosion. According to the Guardian, Kelvin waves are not just waves visible on beaches, but large-scale ocean phenomena that span thousands of miles. When El Niño occurs, the trade winds that originally blow from South America to Asia will weaken or even reverse, causing a large amount of warm sea water accumulated in the western Pacific Ocean to move east along the equator, arrive in South America, and then spread to the north and south, forming Kelvin waves that spread along the coastline. During the epidemic, avoid going to crowded public places and implement measures such as resting at home when sick to reduce the risk of transmission.

59ca3fb65d0a49d99cd6.en:
The Disease Control Agency announced today (18) a new case of local dengue fever, a male in his 30s living in Changhua City, Changhua County. In early September, he sought medical attention for fever symptoms, but the symptoms did not improve. After reporting and testing, he was diagnosed with dengue fever on September 17, and the first type of dengue virus was detected. The case is currently hospitalized, and there are no suspected symptoms in close contacts.

The CDC said that the main place of activity during the incubation period of the case is the home and workplace of Changhua County. There is also a history of activities in neighboring counties and cities. There is no history of foreign travel. It has been determined that the case is a local case. The source of infection remains to be clarified. Relevant health units have carried out emergency chemical control work, vector mosquito density surveys and environmental risk assessments in the vicinity of the case residence or activity site, and strengthened breeding source removal and hygiene education, calling on the public to implement mosquito control measures and cooperate with related prevention and control efforts.

The public should strengthen the prevention of respiratory infectious diseases such as influenza and COVID-19. 2d0976e8f5dda06400e9.en: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) means that the tuberculosis bacteria infected by the patient are at least resistant to the first-line drugs isonicotinamide (INH) and panamycin (RMP), which are classified as the second type of statutory infectious diseases in China. Treatment is more complex than usual tuberculosis, and the efficacy and side effects should be monitored closely and continuously during treatment. In order to optimize the care of drug-resistant tuberculosis patients and avoid the risk of derivative treatment failure and community transmission, the CDC (hereinafter referred to as the CDC) has established a multi-drug-resistant tuberculosis medical care team (Taiwan MDR-TB Consortium, TMTC team) since 2007, integrating medical, public health, testing, pharmaceutical affairs, nursing and other team resources to provide patient treatment drugs at public expense.
